fromContent: Every Daftari write operation auto-commits to git; git is the version-control layer and there is no separate versioning subsystem.
toContent: The .daftari/index.db SQLite file is ephemeral: it is the search/ACL index and can be rebuilt from the markdown files at any time.

fromContent: Daftari's vault_lint reports curation problems but never auto-fixes them; the curation engine is advisory.
toContent: Daftari's vault_tension_log records tensions between documents but never resolves them; recording a tension does not act on it.

fromContent: The cortex scheduler ages each edge with an exponential half-life decay function f(strength); an edge left un-re-examined past its interval becomes due for revision.
toContent: SuperMemo's SM-2 algorithm popularized spaced repetition using an ease factor that lengthens review intervals after each successful recall.

fromContent: Daftari's write locks are file-level, SQLite-backed, with a 60-second TTL; an expired lock is released automatically.
toContent: Only one daftari process may hold a vault at a time; on startup the server SIGTERMs any live daftari holding the per-vault process lock and waits up to 3 seconds before taking over.
subtype: co-occurrence — two locking mechanisms, different layers, orthogonal

fromContent: Multi-head attention lets a transformer attend to information from different representation subspaces in parallel by running several attention heads and concatenating their outputs.
toContent: Transformers add positional encodings to token embeddings because self-attention is permutation-invariant and would otherwise be blind to token order.
subtype: co-occurrence — two transformer components, embedding-near, neither a premise for the other

fromContent: TCP provides reliable, in-order byte-stream delivery using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, and retransmission of lost segments.
toContent: UDP is a connectionless transport that sends datagrams with no delivery guarantee, no ordering, and no built-in retransmission.
subtype: co-occurrence — sibling protocols, often compared, neither derives from the other

fromContent: DNA replication is semiconservative: each daughter double helix retains one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.
toContent: In gene expression, DNA is transcribed into messenger RNA, which ribosomes then translate into a protein.
subtype: co-occurrence — two molecular-biology processes sharing 'DNA', independent

fromContent: Liquid water reaches its maximum density at approximately 4 degrees Celsius.
toContent: At sea-level atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
subtype: co-occurrence — two physical constants of water, independent

fromContent: Gutenberg's printing press, developed around 1440, used reusable movable metal type cast in a hand mould.
toContent: Gutenberg financed his printing enterprise partly through a large loan from the businessman Johann Fust, who later sued him.
subtype: co-occurrence — two facts about Gutenberg's press, independent

fromContent: Mars has two small, irregularly shaped moons, Phobos and Deimos, likely captured asteroids.
toContent: Mars appears reddish because its surface is covered in iron-oxide (rust) dust.

fromContent: English is a West Germanic language within the Indo-European family, descended from the dialects of Anglo-Saxon settlers.
toContent: After the 1066 Norman Conquest, English borrowed thousands of words from Norman French, especially in law, cuisine, and governance.
subtype: co-occurrence — genetic classification vs lexical borrowing, independent

fromContent: Convolutional layers share a small set of weights across all spatial positions, giving the network approximate translation equivariance.
toContent: Pooling layers downsample feature maps, reducing spatial resolution and giving local translation invariance.
subtype: co-occurrence — two CNN components, embedding-near, independent

fromContent: Graphite and diamond are both allotropes of carbon, differing only in how their carbon atoms are bonded and arranged.
toContent: Diamond is the hardest known naturally occurring material, scoring 10 on the Mohs scale.
subtype: co-occurrence — same entity (carbon/diamond), but hardness not derived from allotropy

fromContent: The Adam optimizer adapts a per-parameter learning rate using running estimates of the first and second moments of the gradients.
toContent: Dropout regularizes a network by randomly zeroing a fraction of activations during each training step, reducing co-adaptation.
subtype: co-occurrence — two training techniques, share 'training', independent

fromContent: Daftari's RBAC is config-driven: users and roles are declared in .daftari/config.yaml, and there is no separate user-management system.
toContent: All Daftari content is markdown with YAML frontmatter; the frontmatter is the metadata layer and there is no separate metadata format.
subtype: co-occurrence — access-control config vs content format, orthogonal design decisions

fromContent: Comparative advantage holds that a country gains from specializing in goods for which it has the lowest opportunity cost, even if it is worse at producing everything.
toContent: Absolute advantage describes a country being able to produce a good using fewer inputs than another country.
subtype: co-occurrence — two trade concepts, often compared, neither a premise for the other

fromContent: Precision is the fraction of predicted-positive items that are actually positive (true positives over predicted positives).
toContent: Recall is the fraction of actually-positive items that are predicted positive (true positives over actual positives).
subtype: co-occurrence — paired metrics, defined over the same confusion matrix, neither derives from the other

fromContent: Sound travels through dry air at about 343 metres per second at 20 degrees Celsius.
toContent: Light travels through a vacuum at about 299,792 kilometres per second, the universal speed limit c.
subtype: co-occurrence — two wave-speed facts; shared theme 'speed of X', no derivation (control for loose topical match)
